facts.text: My own kidneys failed completely because of a congenital kidney condition called oligomeganephronia.
I had a kidney transplant from a living donor 20 years ago.
An 8-cm clear cell carcinoma, a kidney cancer, was recently found in my transplanted kidney.
I used to take cyclosporine for the transplant, but it was stopped 29 days ago after the cancer was found.
I also took prednisone for the transplant; it was stopped at the same time, 29 days ago.
Six days ago I had my first dose of nivolumab.
I had my first dose of ipilimumab at the same time, six days ago.

gold.reasoning: 1. Considered acute allograft rejection — “Given the sudden decrease in kidney function in the context of recently discontinuing immunosuppression, starting immunotherapy, and the presence of graft-site tenderness, his presentation was felt to be most suspicious for acute allograft rejection…” 2. Considered renal vein thrombosis — “CT of the abdomen and pelvis … showed … transplant renal vein findings consistent with tumor thrombus, and a subsequent ultrasound confirmed a near occlusive thrombus in the transplant renal vein.” 3. Considered tumor lysis syndrome — “There was no laboratory evidence of tumor lysis syndrome.”
